question.text: The average net profit requirement for a mutual fund sponsor over the preceding five years is:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (p.63) requires the sponsor to have an average net annual profit, after depreciation, interest and tax, of at least Rs. 10 crore during the immediately preceding five years. This profitability test sits alongside the other sponsor-eligibility criteria. The Trap: Rs. 50 crore is the AMC net-worth requirement at p.65, not the sponsor's profit criterion. Candidates frequently swap the sponsor profit number with the AMC net-worth number. Note: Anchor the two figures from the workbook: sponsor — Rs. 10 crore average net annual profit over five years (p.63); AMC — Rs. 50 crore net worth (p.65).
